props.title: Corporate

sections.content: Corporate represents a pivotal moment in Indian cinema's examination of business ethics and workplace dynamics. Director Madhur Bhandarkar crafts a scathing critique of corporate culture that shares DNA with Oliver Stone's Wall Street (1987) and more recent films like Margin Call (2011). Bipasha Basu's portrayal of Nishigandha Dasgupta captures the moral compromises and personal costs of climbing the corporate ladder, while the film's exploration of corruption and power dynamics anticipated later works like The Big Short (2015).

sections.content: The corporate thriller genre gained new relevance in the wake of the 2008 financial crisis. Films like The Company Men (2010) and Too Big to Fail (2011) directly addressed the human impact of corporate collapse, while international films like Corporate and The Other Side of the Street (2004) brought fresh perspectives to workplace power dynamics. These films share common threads of moral ambiguity, systemic corruption, and the personal toll of corporate ambition. SUBHEAD: The Evolution of Workplace Drama

Recent entries in the genre have shifted focus from pure corporate malfeasance to broader workplace issues. Up in the Air (2009) examined the dehumanizing aspects of corporate downsizing, while Sorry to Bother You (2018) used surrealist elements to critique modern capitalism. The success of these films demonstrates audiences' continued appetite for stories that decode and critique corporate culture.
